chunks: Ali ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, he said: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar narrated to us, he said: Muhammad ibn Hassan al-Razi narrated to us, he said: Muhammad ibn Ali al-Kufi narrated to us, he said: Abdullah ibn Jibla narrated from Ali ibn Abu Hamza, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I said to him: May I be sacrificed for you, when is the emergence of the Qa'im? He said: O Abu Muhammad, we, the Ahl al-Bayt, do not specify times, and Muhammad (peace be upon him) has said: 'The time-servers have lied.' O Abu Muhammad, before this matter there are five signs: the first is the call in the month of Ramadan, the emergence of al-Sufyani, the emergence of al-Khurāsani, the killing of al-Nafs al-Zakiyya, and the sinking in al-Bayda'. Then he said: O Abu Muhammad, it is necessary that before that there be two plagues: the white plague and the red plague. I said: May I be sacrificed for you, and what are they? He said: As for the white plague, it is the torrential death, and as for the red plague, it is the sword. And the Qa'im does not emerge until his name is called out from the throat of the sky on the twenty-third night of Ramadan, which is a Friday night. I said: With what will he be called? He said: With his name and his father's name: 'Behold, So-and-so son of So-and-so is the Qa'im of the Family of Muhammad, so listen to him and obey him.' And nothing that Allah created with a spirit will remain but that it hears the shout, so the sleeper awakens and goes out to his courtyard, and the virgin goes out from her veil, and the Qa'im emerges from what he hears, and it is the shout of Gabriel (peace be upon him).

key_terms.السُّفْيَانِي: Al-Sufyani, a specific figure whose emergence is a major sign of the end times
key_terms.الطَّاعُونُ الْأَبْيَضُ: The white plague, interpreted here as a massive death toll
key_terms.الطَّاعُونُ الْأَحْمَرُ: The red plague, interpreted here as war by the sword
key_terms.النَّفْسُ الزَّكِيَّةُ: Al-Nafs al-Zakiyya (The Pure Soul), a figure to be killed before the Imam's emergence
key_terms.الْبَيْدَاءُ: Al-Bayda', a desert region where a sinking (khasf) will occur
key_terms.الْخُرَاسَانِي: Al-Khurāsani, a companion of the Imam who rises in Khurasan
key_terms.الْقَائِم: The Qa'im (The Riser), a title for the Twelfth Imam in Shia eschatology
key_terms.جَوْفِ السَّمَاءِ: The throat of the sky, referring to the source of the divine call

ai.seo_question: What are the five signs and two plagues preceding the emergence of Imam al-Qa'im?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Nu'mani’s *Kitab al-Ghayba* emphasizes the Ahl al-Bayt’s principle of 'not timing' (la naqtu) the reappearance, distinguishing their eschatology from precise chronological speculation. It details five major signs and two preceding plagues—interpreted as widespread death and war—culminating in the celestial call (Nida') by Gabriel in Ramadan, which awakens all creation to the Imam’s authority.
